page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.xlarge is a member of the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6149 processor, running at a clock frequency of 3.1 GHz. The platform allocates 8.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

In terms of peripheral infrastructure, the ecs.hfc5.xlarge does not include dedicated local storage volumes or GPU accelerators. Operating environments and persistent file stores rely entirely on remote network storage volumes. For external communication, the server features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not bundled with the instance deployment.

The hardware profile represents a compute-dense allocation model, trading off local disk capacity and large memory footprints for dedicated processor cycles at high clock frequencies. From an efficiency standpoint, environments that do not require high memory-per-core ratios avoid paying for idle memory overhead. The instance is suited for compute-constrained workloads such as application compilation, API gateways, web serving, continuous integration runners, and front-end microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.xlarge is a compute-focused instance type within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 4 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated hardware GPUs or local storage disks, requiring external cloud block storage for operating systems and persistent data. Networking provisions include a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource ratio targets tasks where processor speed and dedicated compute execution outweigh large memory or massive local storage demands. This hardware profile is appropriate for batch processing, compilation tasks, web serving, and compute-oriented microservices.
